newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Dollar rallies after Colombian central bank ruse.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rallies after Colombian central bank ruse.

text.p: The dollar rose 1.5 pesos to 1,011 pesos when Colombia's central bank threw a dummy punch, fooling traders into thinking it was about to step in.

The dollar appeared to be continuing its six day slide as it sank to an intraday low of 1,005 pesos before the central bank flashed a message across electronic trading screens offering to snap up greenbacks.
"The actions of the central bank had a psychological effect more than anything else because it offered to buy dollars at 1,005 and that forced the dollar back up," one interbank dealer said.
Traders said the bank had not actually intervened in the market. Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
"It was just a trick so that the value of the dollar didn't continue falling," another trader said.

The dollar fell to an intraday low of 1,005 before midday, its lowest level since January 11 as buyers showed little interest in the greenbacks industry was pumping into the market. The central bank ploy pushed rates up to an intraday high of 1,013.5 pesos per dollar.
"The days figures seem a bit artificial to me given that by mid-morning only $60 dollars had been traded," another dealer said.
